speaker: SPEAKER_01
transcript: Well, you know, one of my passions in Congress has been about ending hunger in this country. We live in the richest country in the history of the world, and yet there are 35 million of our fellow citizens who don't know where the next meal is going to come from. And in 1969, the White House actually did a conference on this topic. And out of that came the WIC program, the women's infants and children's program, the modern day food stamp program, more focus on child nutrition, even labeling so that we go shopping, we know what we're buying, and we could tell whether it's good for us or not. And then we start to make progress toward any hunger. And then in the 1980s, and since then, we have started to backslide. And again, tens of millions of our fellow citizens are hungry. And we can do something about it. It's a solvable problem. And I tried to get the Obama administration to do another White House conference, and they did some good stuff, but we didn't get to the point where they did a conference. And then we had four years of Trump, and I said, forget about it. And then when Biden won, we started to reach out to him even before he was sworn in. And to his credit, he and the vice president hosted this conference. And it was really magnificent. I mean, it was about laying out a strategy so we could actually end hunger in this country. And we could end diet related diseases. And we could promote better access to nutrition for everybody. And we talked about things like universal free school meals for all of our children. We talked about enhancing the SNAP program. And we talked about medically tailored meals and that food is medicine. My grandmother used to say to me all the time, an apple a day keeps the doctor away. It would annoy me. I wish she was still alive as I could say, you were right. I mean, our health care system is divorced from nutrition and food. Our education system is we need to rethink this. And this conference is a first big step toward doing that.
